newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No EU decision on BA, American deal before UK vote.
newsitem.headline: No EU decision on BA, American deal before UK vote.

text.p: The European Commission is unlikely to rule on the alliance between British Airways and AMR Corp's American Airlines before the British general election on May 1, EU sources said on Tuesday.
"You won't hear from us before May 1," one source said.

The comment was something of a surprise given that the EU commissioners in charge of competition and air transport, Karel Van Miert and Neil Kinnock, said on February 25 that a decision was expected in weeks rather than months.

But the Commission now appears more concerned about not taking any controversial decisions that may influence the British electoral debate already hijacked by many controversial EU issues like the creation of a single European currency.
"We are not going to fuel what is going to be an awful debate," the source said.

The Commission is also in less of a hurry to reach a decision on the planned link-up between BA and American now that the British authorities themselves are moving more cautiously on the issue and cooperating a lot more with its antitrust officials, the sources said.

In January, the alliance ran into strong opposition from the Commission, and particularly Van Miert who argued it would eliminate competition on 13 routes between the United Kingdom and the United States.

Commission and industry sources have stressed that Britain is now cooperating more with the EU's competition watchdog than at the end of last year when the Office of Fair Trading proposed clearing the deal provided the companies gave up 168 weekly slots at London Heathrow airport.

Problems in agreeing a so-called bilateral 'open skies' agreement between the U.S. and Britain -- which the authorities on the other side of the Atlantic have said is a pre-condition for the alliance -- have apparently contributed to the delays.
Speculation has also been mounting in Britain that the government itself will not approve the operation before the general elections.
Van Miert warned Britain again last month against clearing the alliance without first properly addressing the Commission's concerns about its impact on competition.

The Commission considers that the deal would strengthen BA's and American's dominant position on the UK-U.S. routes and is seeking guarantees that rival EU carriers will not be excluded from those routes.
It particularly wants slots at congested Heathrow to be surrendered, not sold, as suggested by the companies.
